name: ChibiHash
workload: SMHasher3 speed test: large-buffer bulk hashing (GiB/sec) and small-key latency (cycles/hash) for 1-32 byte keys
claimed_speedup: chibihash64: 24.20 GiB/s bulk vs xxhash64's 15.10 and city64's 18.30 (~1.3-1.6x); 34 cycles/hash small-key vs xxhash64's 50 and spooky64's 70 (README benchmark table, made via smhasher3)
tradeoffs: minimal mixing means weaker collision resistance than xxhash64; not for adversarial/hash-flooding contexts; no SIMD/hardware-specific instructions so portability is a design goal, not raw peak speed
caveats: README table gives no compiler/CPU model (says 'made via smhasher3'); v1 failed 3 smhasher3 tests, v2 (current) passes all 252; no LICENSE file in repo, README states 'released into the public domain' (no patent grant)
found_via: GitHub: gh api graphql repo search "chibihash" (surfaced via HN Algolia lead on non-crypto hash functions), opened github.com/N-R-K/ChibiHash README

name: a5hash
workload: Small-key (1-32 byte, hash-table/hash-map style) hashing latency; also author's own repeated 0-64 byte hashing on Zen 5 and bulk hashing on Ryzen 9950X
claimed_speedup: SMHasher3: a5hash small-key avg 26.91 cycles/hash vs wyhash's 29.31 and xxhash64's 52.60 (~8% and ~49% faster respectively); author's own README claims ~11 cycles/hash for 0-64 byte strings on Zen 5 and 15 GB/s bulk on Ryzen 9950X (different methodology, not cross-checked against a specific baseline number)
hardware: Zen 5 / Ryzen 9950X (author's own numbers); unstated in SMHasher3 summary table
tradeoffs: plain a5hash() bulk throughput (2.63 bytes/cycle in SMHasher3) is lower than wyhash's (6.98) - it is optimized specifically for small-key latency, not bulk; a5hash128 variant trades some small-key speed for much higher bulk throughput (6.92 bytes/cycle); non-portable hash values across endianness by design
caveats: same author as komihash (already catalogued, excluded here); SMHasher3 summary page states no compiler/CPU; author's headline cycle/throughput numbers are from a different, uncontrolled benchmark than the SMHasher3 table
found_via: GitHub: gh api graphql repo search "a5hash", opened github.com/avaneev/a5hash README and SMHasher3 results page

name: MuseAir (C++ port)
workload: SMHasher3 small-key (1-31 byte) and bulk (262144-byte) speed tests, run on a 12th Gen Intel i7-12700K, comparing MuseAir/MuseAir-BFast against wyhash and rapidhash
claimed_speedup: "MuseAir in C++ ... clocking in at up to 33.2 GiB/s for the BFast variant"; README states it "holds its own against" wyhash, with charts (not machine-readable numbers) comparing cycles/hash and GiB/s vs wyhash and rapidhash
tradeoffs: requires C++20; header-only but with platform-specific assembly on critical paths; this is a third-party reimplementation, not the canonical original (eternal-io/museair, Rust, no stated license)
caveats: the only exact number stated in text is the absolute 33.2 GiB/s figure, not a head-to-head ratio; the actual wyhash-comparison numbers live in PNG charts in the repo that were not machine-read; README's own license badge says MIT at the top but GitHub reports the repo's actual LICENSE file as GPL-3.0 (used GPL-3.0 per API)
found_via: GitHub: gh api graphql repo search "MuseAir hash", opened github.com/Twilight-Dream-Of-Magic/museair-cpp README

name: Meow hash
workload: SMHasher3 bulk speed test on large (262144-byte) buffers, AES-NI-accelerated
claimed_speedup: 12.43 bytes/cycle bulk vs xxHash-64's 3.99, CityHash-64's 4.75 and wyhash's 6.98 (SMHasher3 results table) - roughly 1.8-3x higher bulk throughput
hardware: requires x86-64 AES-NI (no specific CPU model stated in the SMHasher3 summary page)
tradeoffs: much worse small-key latency (61.5 cycles/hash vs wyhash's 29.3); after a published cryptanalysis break the maintainer downgraded it from security level 3 to level 1 and now recommends against using it for hash tables where hash-flooding/DoS is a concern; requires AES-NI hardware; project stalled at v0.5 'proposal' status, never reached v1.0
caveats: designed and best suited for large-buffer/bulk hashing (e.g. asset/file hashing), not small-key hash-table use where it loses to wyhash/xxHash; official landing page (mollyrocket.com/meowhash) is a stub with no benchmark data, so SMHasher3 is the only numeric source used here
found_via: GitHub: HN Algolia search "non-cryptographic hash function" -> Meow Hash story -> gh api graphql repo search "meow_hash", opened github.com/cmuratori/meow_hash README and SMHasher3 results page

name: AquaHash
workload: Bulk hashing throughput (AES-intrinsics-based); README's own graph also covers small-key sizes vs xxhash64 and FarmHash on Skylake
claimed_speedup: SMHasher3: 15.84 bytes/cycle bulk vs xxHash-64's 3.99 and wyhash's 6.98 (~2.3-4x); own README: "substantially outperforms most common hash functions at all key sizes", ~15 bytes/cycle bulk, graph vs xxhash64 and FarmHash on Skylake
hardware: Intel Skylake (author's own graph); unstated in SMHasher3 summary table
tradeoffs: requires AES-NI intrinsics; header-only C++; same author as MetroHash (jandrewrogers, checked separately but had no usable numeric benchmark)
caveats: fails 55 of ~250 SMHasher3 statistical quality tests - notable quality concern despite speed; predates wyhash (2019 release); no commits since 2019 (never reached a stated v2.0); own comparison graph doesn't state compiler/flags
found_via: GitHub: gh api graphql repo search "aquahash", opened github.com/jandrewrogers/AquaHash README and SMHasher3 results page
